title: Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target Array
corePattern: Greedy Vertical Counting / Painting Fence with Positive Differences
interviewTips: Clarify operation: increment any contiguous subarray by 1, starting from all zeros, ask for minimum operations to reach target.
Trade-off: simulation is intuitive but O(n * max) time, divide and conquer shows structure O(n log n) average, greedy single pass is O(n) optimal with O(1) space.
Edge cases: single element, strictly decreasing array needs only target[0] ops, strictly increasing needs target[-1] ops, large values up to 1e5 require 64-bit safe accumulation logic.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Simulation
approaches.intuition: Build target forward step by step. While current array differs, take the leftmost unfinished position, extend as far as possible over unfinished positions, increment that whole segment by 1. Each increment is one allowed operation, so counting steps gives answer.
approaches.theory: Any optimal solution can be transformed to use maximal extendable segments greedily without extra cost for simulation. Reverse view is decrementing target to zero by decrementing subarrays. Forward simulation is correct but slow because it performs exactly answer many iterations, each scanning O(n). Answer can be sum(target) up to 1e10, so this is exponential in input size and only for understanding.

timeComplexity.explanation: S is answer = up to sum(target). Each operation scans O(n) to find segment and update. Worst O(n * max(target)) e.g., n=1e5, max=1e5 is infeasible. Demonstrates why optimization needed.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Extra cur array of size n to simulate building, plus O(1) pointers.

edgeCases: n=1 needs target[0] ops, many loops
decreasing [3,2,1] still needs 3 ops but simulation does 3 iterations
all zeros not allowed by constraints but would need 0 ops

approaches.name: Approach 2: Divide and Conquer on Minimum
approaches.intuition: If we must raise interval [l,r] from height base to target heights, we can raise whole interval to its minimum, then solve left and right parts independently. Minimum splits problem because operations covering across minimum can be shared.
approaches.theory: Let m be index of minimum in [l,r]. Need target[m]-base operations that cover m, they can also cover everything else in [l,r] for free. After applying them, left [l,m-1] and right [m+1,r] have new base target[m] and are independent since any further operation cannot cross m without overshooting m. Recurrence: F(l,r,base)=target[m]-base+F(l,m-1,target[m])+F(m+1,r,target[m]). Correct by induction.

timeComplexity.complexity: O(n log n) average, O(n^2) worst
timeComplexity.explanation: Each level scans to find minimum. Balanced splits give n log n, sorted array gives n + (n-1) + ... = O(n^2). Can be improved to O(n log n) worst with segment tree or sparse table.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion depth up to n for sorted input, plus O(n) input. Average depth O(log n).

steps: right solve(2,3,1): min at 2 val=1 cost=0 + solve(3,3,1)=1 -> total 1

edgeCases: strictly increasing causes O(n^2) degenerate recursion
all equal: one minimum split still O(n^2) naive scan, answer = value
deep recursion may stack overflow for n=1e5 in Python/Java

approaches.name: Approach 3: Greedy Single Pass with Monotonic Stack Insight
approaches.intuition: Operations can be carried over from previous position. If target[i] <= target[i-1], the operations used for previous already cover current, no new ops needed. If target[i] > target[i-1], need exactly the difference as new operations starting at i.
approaches.theory: Consider building left to right maintaining a monotonic stack of heights. Number of active increments needed at i is target[i]. At step i, we keep min(target[i], target[i-1]) shared operations continuing, and add max(0, target[i]-target[i-1]) new ones. Telescoping sum gives target[0] + sum positive diffs. This equals stack solution where we push increasing heights and pop decreasing heights, counting pushes. Optimal by exchange argument: any solution needs at least that many distinct starts.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single linear scan, each element visited once with O(1) work.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only accumulator and loop index. Explicit monotonic stack version would use O(n) worst but same time.

edgeCases: alternating [1,100000,1,100000] -> large sum fits 32-bit int but use long for safety
